newsitem.title: USA: DAKA faces class action suit - lawyers.
newsitem.headline: DAKA faces class action suit - lawyers.

text.p: DAKA International Inc shareholders filed a class action lawsuit against the company alleging the company violated the U.S. Securities Exchange Act, the plaintiffs' lawyers said on Friday.

The complaint charged DAKA and Chairman and Chief Executive Officer William Baumhauer with allegedly misrepresenting and omitting material information about the company's same-store sales results and the future business prospects of its Fuddruckers Inc restaurant chain during the class period.
The company declined to comment until it had been served notice of the lawsuit.

The suit was filed on behalf of people who purchased or otherwise acquired the DAKA International securities between October 30, 1995 and September 9, 1996, the so-called class period, the lawyers said.

The complaint said the defendants allegedly "recklessly disregarded" the fact that DAKA was experiencing serious problems and trends in its Fuddruckers business that hampered its ability to meet company growth targets, the lawyers said.
Defendants allegedly cited poor winter weather to explain negative same-store sales results at the chain, the lawyers said, adding that plaintiffs sought to recover damages.

But "by the beginning of the class period, defendants knew or recklessly disregarded that there were other serious problems and trends causing Fuddruckers' 'same-store' sales to decline and that such problems and trends were sustained, material and of a nature that would continue to negatively impact Fuddruckers' 'same store' sales results going forward," the lawyers said the suit charged.
The complaint also said the defendants' alleged "scheme" drove DAKA's share price higher during the class period, the lawyers said.

On October 16, DAKA said it expected to post a net first quarter loss of between $0.35 and $0.40 per share. It said Fuddruckers was continuing to hold back performance although it was taking steps to improve the unit's performance.
DAKA also said it expected the chain to become profitable in the second quarter and for the remainder of the year.
The plaintiffs were represented by the law firms of Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach LLP, Shapiro Haber & Urmy LLP and Alfred G. Yates Jr.
